<description>
The depends packages are built without `_FORTIFY_SOURCE` and `-fstack-clash-protection` unless the compiler turns them on by default. `CMakeLists.txt` adds both to `core_interface` only. The release flags in `depends/hosts/linux.mk` and `mingw32.mk` are only `-O2`. Debian's GCC turns on neither, so sqlite, libzmq and capnp are built without them. #27118 built libevent with `-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3`, but libevent is no longer in depends.

I add `-U_FORTIFY_SOURCE -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3 -fstack-clash-protection` to `linux_release_CFLAGS`, and the two `_FORTIFY_SOURCE` flags to `mingw32_release_CFLAGS`. Through `toolchain.cmake` the flags also reach the main build. There secp256k1, which does not link `core_interface`, gets them too. #36534 does that for every build. Qt 6.8 already adds both flags to its own targets on Linux. I leave macOS alone, because its SDK already fortifies. Apple clang 21 ignores `-fstack-clash-protection` on arm64. I did not add `-fcf-protection` (see #30685).

In a `debian:trixie` container (GCC 14.2, aarch64) I built depends with `NO_QT=1` and then Core, on master and on this branch. On master no library in depends calls a `_chk` function. On this branch `libsqlite3.a`, `libzmq.a`, `libkj.a`, `libkj-async.a` and `libcapnpc.a` do. secp256k1 is compiled with the new flags. All 380 ctest tests pass, and so do `interface_zmq.py`, `wallet_basic.py` and `wallet_backup.py`. With `HOST=x86_64-w64-mingw32ucrt` (mingw-w64 12), `libsqlite3.a` calls `__memcpy_chk` and `bitcoind.exe` links. I have not run a Guix build or built Qt.

This is one of several PRs from a large audit of Bitcoin Core that I did with the help of LLM tools. The audit produced its evidence all at once, which is why the PRs arrive together. I understand each change fully and will answer review questions myself.
</description>

<commits>
4d9443b461 depends: harden Linux and Windows packages

The release flags for Linux and Windows packages are only -O2. So
sqlite, libzmq, capnp and the others are built without
_FORTIFY_SOURCE, and on Linux without -fstack-clash-protection,
unless the compiler turns them on by default. Debian's GCC turns on
neither.

Add -U_FORTIFY_SOURCE -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3 to linux_release_CFLAGS and
mingw32_release_CFLAGS, and -fstack-clash-protection to
linux_release_CFLAGS. CMakeLists.txt adds the same flags to
core_interface. toolchain.cmake passes them to the main build as well,
so secp256k1 also gets them in depends builds.

Leave macOS alone: its SDK already fortifies, and Apple clang ignores
-fstack-clash-protection on arm64.
</commits>

diff --git a/depends/hosts/linux.mk b/depends/hosts/linux.mk
